title.narrative: Improving the Core Functions of Primary Care in Sub-Saharan Africa

description.narrative:
Research Aim and Objectives The study aims to use the regional version of the PCAT for sub-Saharan Africa to measure, compare, and improve the core functions of primary care across multiple country contexts. Specific objectives:
1. To develop the PCAT in appropriate languages with support for data collection, analysis and reporting. 2. To measure the core functions of primary care in eleven sub-Saharan African countries. 3. To engage local stakeholders in the PCAT findings and plan interventions to improve the quality of primary care. 4. To engage regional stakeholders in the use of PCAT as part of a package of measurement tools for countries in sub-Saharan Africa.

The study will include adult primary care users (18+) who have visited their facility at least three times in the past year, ensuring familiarity with services. Participants will be selected via systematic random sampling, stratified by monthly patient numbers to cover different facility types and sizes.

This project uses a validated regional Primary Care Assessment Tool (PCAT) to measure the five core functions of primary health care from patientsâ€™ perspectives across eleven sub-Saharan African countries. It includes multi-language surveys and stakeholder engagement to co-design district-level quality improvement plans. The findings will support benchmarking, policy engagement, and efforts to strengthen PHC systems toward universal health coverage and the SDGs.

activity-date.narrative: The study officially began in September, in Zambia, with preparatory activities including translation of the Primary Care Assessment Tool (PCAT), stakeholder engagement, ethical submissions and seeking permission from respective Government Departments to conduct the study.

recipient-country.narrative: The study in Zambia will be conducted in Chongwe District of Lusaka Province.

name.narrative: Chongwe District, in Lusaka Province of Zambia

description.narrative: Chongwe District is a rapidly growing district in Lusaka Province, located just east of Lusaka. It combines rural and peri-urban characteristics, with expanding residential and commercial development along the Great East Road. Bordering Kafue, Rufunsa, and Luangwa districts, Chongwe also has about 41 public health facilities, including health centres, health posts, and a district hospital, supported by several private clinics.

sector.narrative: The PCAT Project, implemented by the University of Zambia, strengthens primary health care by assessing service quality, accessibility, and coordination to inform policy and improve delivery. The project generates evidence, builds local capacity, and supports health system planning and performance monitoring in Zambia.
